glossary.definition: Transmission of traits from parents to offspring through genes.
Differences among individuals of a species in inherited characteristics.
Trait expressed even when only one copy of the allele is present.
Trait expressed only when two copies of the allele are present.
Mendelian cross involving one pair of contrasting traits.
Cross involving two pairs of contrasting traits studied by Mendel.
Genetic makeup of an organism (e.g. Tt, TT, tt).
Observable physical expression of traits (e.g. tall, violet flowers).

concepts.name: What is heredity?
concepts.simple_answer: Heredity is the transmission of traits from parents to offspring through genetic information in DNA.
concepts.example: Children resemble parents in eye colour and blood group.
concepts.remember: Offspring inherit instructions from both parents in sexual reproduction.
concepts.common_confusion: Heredity is not same as growth alone.

concepts.name: Inherited traits examples
concepts.simple_answer: Traits like eye colour, hair texture, earlobe attachment, and blood group pass from parents to children.
concepts.example: Free vs attached earlobe varies in family.
concepts.common_confusion: Not all resemblance is genetic — learned behaviour differs.

concepts.name: Acquired vs inherited (recap)
concepts.simple_answer: Inherited traits are in DNA at birth; acquired traits develop during life and are not passed genetically.
concepts.example: NCERT mice tail-cutting experiment shows acquired not inherited.
concepts.remember: Only germ cell DNA changes affect offspring.
concepts.common_confusion: Weight from overeating is not inherited trait.

concepts.name: Rules of heredity — historical question
concepts.simple_answer: For centuries people wondered if traits blend in offspring or pass as discrete units — Mendel answered with experiments.
concepts.example: Children are not exact average of parents.
concepts.remember: Discrete traits follow patterns Mendel found.

concepts.name: Gregor Mendel
concepts.simple_answer: Gregor Mendel, Austrian monk, used pea plants in garden experiments to discover laws of inheritance.
concepts.example: Pea plants easy to grow; many visible traits.
concepts.common_confusion: Called father of genetics.

concepts.name: Why pea plants?
concepts.simple_answer: Pea plants self-pollinate, grow fast, have contrasting traits (tall/dwarf, green/yellow seeds) easy to count.
concepts.common_confusion: Many offspring per cross.

concepts.name: Contrasting characters in pea
concepts.simple_answer: Mendel studied seven pairs: tall/dwarf, round/wrinkled seed, yellow/green seed, etc.
concepts.example: Round yellow seeds vs wrinkled green.
concepts.remember: Each trait had two clear forms.
concepts.common_confusion: Know at least four pairs for exam.

concepts.name: Gene and allele preview
concepts.simple_answer: Gene controls a trait; alleles are different forms of a gene (e.g. tall allele vs dwarf allele).
concepts.example: T and t represent tall and dwarf alleles.
concepts.remember: Offspring gets one allele from each parent.
concepts.common_confusion: Uppercase often dominant — formal day later.

concepts.name: Sexual reproduction and heredity
concepts.simple_answer: Two parents each contribute one allele per gene — offspring has new combination.
concepts.example: Human has 23 chromosome pairs — one set from each parent.
concepts.remember: Meiosis halves chromosome number in gametes.

concepts.name: Chapter 8 roadmap
concepts.simple_answer: Ch 8 covers Mendel's experiments, monohybrid and dihybrid crosses, sex determination, blood groups, and Activities 8.1–8.2.

concepts.name: Accumulation of variations
concepts.simple_answer: Variations accumulate over generations through sexual reproduction and occasional DNA changes.
concepts.example: Populations show range of heights, not one value.
concepts.remember: Sexual shuffling adds new combos each generation.
concepts.common_confusion: Evolution acts on accumulated variation.

concepts.name: Importance for species survival
concepts.simple_answer: Species with accumulated variation has better chance some individuals survive environmental change.
concepts.remember: Without variation, one stress kills all.
concepts.common_confusion: Links Ch 7 variation to Ch 8 heredity.

concepts.name: Sexual reproduction and new combinations
concepts.simple_answer: Each generation gets new allele combinations unlike either parent exactly — except identical twins.

concepts.name: Population vs individual
concepts.simple_answer: Heredity studied at individual level (parent-offspring); variation important at population level.
concepts.example: Breeding programmes select from population variation.
concepts.remember: Both levels needed for full picture.

concepts.name: Stable vs changing environment
concepts.simple_answer: Stable environment favours current traits; changing environment favours previously rare beneficial variants.
concepts.example: Antibiotic resistance rises when antibiotics used.

concepts.name: DNA copying errors in inheritance
concepts.simple_answer: Rare copying errors in gamete formation create new alleles passed to offspring if fertilisation occurs.
concepts.example: Most mutations neutral or harmful; few beneficial.

concepts.name: Breeding and artificial selection
concepts.simple_answer: Humans select plants/animals with desired variants to breed — uses heredity and variation principles.
concepts.remember: Same logic as natural selection but human directed.

concepts.name: Limitations of inherited information
concepts.simple_answer: Environment also affects expression — same genotype can differ in phenotype (nutrition affects height).
concepts.example: Identical twins may differ slightly in weight.
concepts.remember: Heredity sets potential; environment affects outcome.

concepts.name: NCERT exercise link — variation
concepts.simple_answer: Review NCERT questions linking variation in reproduction to survival of species.

concepts.name: Variation accumulation summary
concepts.simple_answer: Sexual reproduction shuffles and accumulates variations; populations with diversity survive change better.
concepts.example: Link Ch 7 DNA copying to Ch 8 patterns.

concepts.name: Mendel's monohybrid experiment
concepts.simple_answer: Mendel crossed pea plants differing in one trait (e.g. tall × dwarf) and tracked offspring traits.
concepts.example: P generation pure lines; F1 all tall in classic cross.
concepts.remember: Counted thousands of plants for ratios.
concepts.common_confusion: One trait at a time — monohybrid.

concepts.name: P generation
concepts.simple_answer: P (parental) generation uses pure breeding homozygous plants — tall × tall always tall before cross.

concepts.name: F1 generation result
concepts.simple_answer: F1 offspring of tall × dwarf cross were all tall — dwarf seemed to disappear.
concepts.common_confusion: Cross between contrasting P parents.

concepts.name: F2 generation result
concepts.simple_answer: F1 self-pollinated → F2 showed both tall and dwarf in approximately 3:1 ratio.
concepts.common_confusion: Large sample gave statistical ratio.

concepts.name: Law of Dominance
concepts.simple_answer: When two contrasting alleles combine, one (dominant) expresses in F1; other (recessive) hidden but can return in F2.
concepts.example: Tall allele T dominant over t.
concepts.common_confusion: Recessive needs two copies to show.

concepts.name: Law of Segregation
concepts.simple_answer: Alleles separate during gamete formation so each gamete carries only one allele per gene.
concepts.example: Tt plant makes T and t gametes in equal proportion.
concepts.common_confusion: Segregation happens in meiosis.

concepts.name: Activity 8.1 — monohybrid cross simulation
concepts.simple_answer: Activity 8.1 uses beads/cards to simulate allele combinations showing 3:1 F2 ratio.
concepts.example: Random pick two alleles mimics fertilisation.

concepts.name: Mendel's method strength
concepts.simple_answer: Large sample size, one variable at a time, mathematical counting, pure lines — scientific rigour.

concepts.name: Terminology checkpoint
concepts.simple_answer: Define: allele, dominant, recessive, homozygous, heterozygous, genotype, phenotype — formal day next.
concepts.remember: TT and Tt both tall phenotype.

concepts.name: Mendel rules summary
concepts.simple_answer: Dominance explains F1 uniformity; segregation explains F2 3:1 ratio; gametes carry one allele each.
concepts.example: State both laws with pea example.

concepts.name: Punnett square — purpose
concepts.simple_answer: Punnett square diagram predicts offspring genotypes and phenotypes from parent gametes.
concepts.common_confusion: Named after Reginald Punnett.

concepts.name: Gamete formation for Tt
concepts.simple_answer: Heterozygous Tt produces 50% T gametes and 50% t gametes — segregation.
concepts.example: Write T and t on one parent side of square.

concepts.name: Cross Tt × Tt
concepts.simple_answer: Both parents heterozygous tall: gametes T and t each; offspring TT, Tt, tT, tt.
concepts.remember: Genotype ratio differs from phenotype ratio.

concepts.name: Genotype vs phenotype
concepts.simple_answer: Genotype is genetic makeup (TT, Tt, tt); phenotype is observable trait (tall or dwarf).
concepts.example: Tt and TT both tall phenotype.
concepts.common_confusion: Blood group phenotype from genotype.

concepts.name: Homozygous vs heterozygous
concepts.simple_answer: Homozygous: same alleles (TT or tt). Heterozygous: different alleles (Tt).
concepts.example: TT homozygous dominant; tt homozygous recessive.

concepts.name: Test cross (brief)
concepts.simple_answer: Cross unknown dominant with homozygous recessive — if any recessive offspring, unknown was heterozygous.
concepts.example: T? × tt — dwarf offspring means Tt parent.

concepts.name: Probability interpretation
concepts.simple_answer: 3:1 ratio is probabilistic — small families may not match exactly; large numbers approach ratio.

concepts.name: Monohybrid cross problems
concepts.simple_answer: Practice: cross TT×tt, Tt×tt, tt×tt — write genotype and phenotype ratios each.

concepts.name: Human monohybrid examples
concepts.simple_answer: Some traits simplified as monohybrid for teaching — earlobe attachment, widow's peak (simplified models).
concepts.example: Real human genetics often more complex.

concepts.name: Monohybrid summary
concepts.simple_answer: Draw Punnett square; gametes on axes; read off 1:2:1 genotype and 3:1 phenotype for Tt×Tt.

concepts.name: Dominant allele expression
concepts.simple_answer: Dominant allele expresses its trait in phenotype when at least one copy present (TT or Tt).
concepts.common_confusion: Dominant does not mean more common in population.

concepts.name: Recessive allele expression
concepts.simple_answer: Recessive allele shows phenotype only when two copies present (homozygous recessive tt).
concepts.common_confusion: Recessive traits can skip generations.

concepts.name: F1 uniform phenotype explained
concepts.simple_answer: F1 all tall because T from one parent dominates t from other — every F1 is Tt.

concepts.name: F2 separation explained
concepts.simple_answer: F1 Tt self-cross: gametes combine giving TT, Tt, tt in 1:2:1 — tt shows dwarf again.
concepts.example: Recessive reappears when two t gametes meet.

concepts.name: Carrier concept
concepts.simple_answer: Heterozygous individual carries recessive allele without showing trait — called carrier.
concepts.example: Carrier of recessive disease allele healthy but can pass allele.

concepts.name: Pure vs hybrid (Mendel terms)
concepts.simple_answer: Pure breeding = homozygous; hybrid = heterozygous F1 from contrasting parents.

concepts.name: Pedigree preview
concepts.simple_answer: Family tree diagrams track traits across generations — recessive can appear from carrier parents.
concepts.example: Squares male, circles female in standard pedigree.

concepts.name: Why ratios matter
concepts.simple_answer: Predicting ratios helps plant breeding and understanding genetic disease inheritance patterns.
concepts.example: Expect 25% homozygous recessive from carrier × carrier.

concepts.name: Common dominance misconceptions
concepts.simple_answer: Dominant ≠ better or more common; recessive ≠ absent from population; one allele from each parent always.

concepts.name: F1 F2 summary
concepts.simple_answer: F1 heterozygous shows dominant; F2 self-cross restores recessive in 1/4 — dominance + segregation together.
concepts.example: Explain F1 and F2 without memorising only ratio.

concepts.name: Dihybrid cross — definition
concepts.simple_answer: Dihybrid cross tracks inheritance of two traits simultaneously (e.g. seed shape and colour).
concepts.remember: Each trait has own allele pair.

concepts.name: Mendel dihybrid experiment
concepts.simple_answer: Mendel crossed round yellow (RRYY) with wrinkled green (rryy); F1 all round yellow.

concepts.name: F2 dihybrid ratio
concepts.simple_answer: F2 showed 9:3:3:1 phenotype ratio — round-yellow, round-green, wrinkled-yellow, wrinkled-green.

concepts.name: Law of Independent Assortment
concepts.simple_answer: Genes for different traits assort independently during gamete formation if on different chromosome pairs.
concepts.remember: Produces new trait combinations in F2.
concepts.common_confusion: Exception: linked genes on same chromosome — beyond basic.

concepts.name: Dihybrid Punnett square
concepts.simple_answer: 16-box Punnett square for RrYy × RrYy — track both allele pairs together.
concepts.example: Gametes: RY, Ry, rY, ry from each parent.

concepts.name: Gamete types from RrYy
concepts.simple_answer: Heterozygous dihybrid produces four gamete types in equal proportion: RY, Ry, rY, ry.
concepts.example: Each gamete one allele per gene.
concepts.remember: 2^n gamete types for n heterozygous gene pairs.

concepts.name: Why 9:3:3:1
concepts.simple_answer: 9 = both dominant; 3 = one dominant one recessive each way; 1 = both recessive.

concepts.name: Activity 8.2 — dihybrid simulation
concepts.simple_answer: Activity 8.2 simulates dihybrid cross with beads showing approach to 9:3:3:1.
concepts.example: More trials → closer to expected ratio.

concepts.name: Dihybrid problem strategy
concepts.simple_answer: Step 1: identify parent genotypes. Step 2: list gametes. Step 3: Punnett square. Step 4: count phenotypes.

concepts.name: Dihybrid summary
concepts.simple_answer: Independent assortment gives F2 9:3:3:1; four gamete types from RrYy; practice 16-box square.

concepts.name: Sex determination — need
concepts.simple_answer: Mechanism decides whether offspring develops as male or female — species-specific.
concepts.common_confusion: Separate from general body traits inheritance.

concepts.name: Human chromosomes
concepts.simple_answer: Humans have 23 pairs chromosomes — 22 autosome pairs + 1 sex chromosome pair.

concepts.name: XX female, XY male
concepts.simple_answer: Females have XX sex chromosomes; males have XY — male determines sex of child via gamete.
concepts.common_confusion: Sex of baby depends on father's sperm.

concepts.name: Gametes and sex chromosomes
concepts.simple_answer: All egg cells have X chromosome; sperm half carry X and half carry Y.

visual.label: Eggs X; sperm X or Y

concepts.example: XX egg + X sperm → girl; XX egg + Y sperm → boy.

concepts.name: Sex determination is not 'blame'
concepts.simple_answer: Biology shows sex determined at fertilisation by chromosome combination — avoid social misconceptions.
concepts.example: Only one parent contributes Y for male offspring.

concepts.name: Other species examples
concepts.simple_answer: Birds often ZW female ZZ male; some reptiles temperature-dependent — contrast with humans.
concepts.example: Human XY is one system among many.

concepts.name: Sex linked preview
concepts.simple_answer: Genes on X chromosome (e.g. colour blindness) show different inheritance patterns — related topic.
concepts.example: Males XY have one X — express X recessive more.

concepts.name: Punnett for sex determination
concepts.simple_answer: Cross XX × XY on Punnett square gives 50% XX and 50% XY offspring.
concepts.example: Not using T/t — use X and Y symbols.
concepts.remember: No YY viable human — not standard cross.

concepts.name: Misconceptions
concepts.simple_answer: Mother does not 'decide' baby sex in XY system; Y chromosome from father makes male development pathway.
concepts.remember: Old folk beliefs lack chromosome basis.

concepts.name: Sex determination summary
concepts.simple_answer: Human female XX, male XY; sperm X or Y decides; Punnett shows 1:1; know chromosome pair count.
concepts.example: Draw karyotype sketch XX and XY.

concepts.name: ABO blood groups
concepts.simple_answer: Human ABO blood group controlled by gene with alleles Iᴬ, Iᴮ, and i — inherited trait.
concepts.example: Type A, B, AB, O phenotypes.
concepts.common_confusion: Not simple single dominant only.

concepts.name: Multiple alleles
concepts.simple_answer: More than two alleles exist for a gene in population though individual has only two.
concepts.example: Iᴬ and Iᴮ codominant; i recessive.
concepts.remember: You inherit one allele from each parent.

concepts.name: Codominance in AB
concepts.simple_answer: Blood group AB shows both A and B antigens — codominance of Iᴬ and Iᴮ.
concepts.example: AB has neither A nor B dominant over other.

concepts.name: Genotype to phenotype ABO
concepts.simple_answer: IᴬIᴬ or Iᴬi → type A; IᴮIᴮ or Iᴮi → type B; IᴬIᴮ → AB; ii → type O.
concepts.example: Type O is universal donor (RBC) simplified teaching.
concepts.remember: Know parent cross predicts child possibilities.

concepts.name: Blood transfusion compatibility
concepts.simple_answer: Transfusion needs compatible blood groups to avoid clumping — ABO antigen-antibody reaction.
concepts.remember: O donors often universal; AB receivers often universal.
concepts.common_confusion: Rh factor adds another layer.

concepts.name: Rh factor (brief)
concepts.simple_answer: Rh protein on RBC — Rh+ or Rh− inherited separately from ABO.
concepts.example: Rh incompatibility in pregnancy managed medically.
concepts.remember: Positive has Rh protein; negative lacks.

concepts.name: Blood group inheritance problems
concepts.simple_answer: Practice cross: Iᴬi × Iᴮi — possible offspring genotypes and phenotypes with Punnett square.
concepts.example: Child type O from two type A possible if both Iᴬi.
concepts.remember: Show working for medical genetics style Q.

concepts.name: Ethical note — blood donation
concepts.simple_answer: Voluntary blood donation saves lives; know your group; science enables safe matching.
concepts.example: Blood camps in schools and communities.

concepts.name: Blood group vs Mendel pea
concepts.simple_answer: ABO shows codominance and multiple alleles — extends basic dominant/recessive pea model.
concepts.example: Not all traits follow single T/t pattern.
concepts.remember: Peas teach foundation; blood groups add complexity.

concepts.name: Blood groups summary
concepts.simple_answer: ABO: Iᴬ, Iᴮ, i alleles; codominance AB; practice inheritance problems; transfusion compatibility.

concepts.name: Family resemblance
concepts.simple_answer: Children inherit combination of traits from both parents — explains resemblance and differences among siblings.
concepts.example: Nose shape may resemble one parent; hair another.

concepts.name: Single gene traits (teaching examples)
concepts.simple_answer: Earlobe attachment, rolling tongue, widow's peak taught as simplified inherited examples.
concepts.remember: Real genetics may involve multiple genes.

concepts.name: Hidden recessive traits
concepts.simple_answer: Recessive traits skip generations when carriers marry carriers — appears in quarter of children on average.

concepts.name: Dominant traits in pedigree
concepts.simple_answer: Dominant traits appear every generation if allele present — unless new mutation.
concepts.example: Affected child usually has affected parent for dominant.
concepts.remember: Exceptions: new mutation or non-paternity rare.

concepts.name: Identical vs fraternal twins
concepts.simple_answer: Identical (monozygotic) same genotype; fraternal (dizygotic) like siblings born together.
concepts.remember: Fraternal twins can be opposite sex.

concepts.name: Sex-linked colour blindness
concepts.simple_answer: Red-green colour blindness often X-linked recessive — more common in males with one X.
concepts.example: Carrier mother can pass to son.
concepts.remember: Males XY express X recessive directly.

concepts.name: Genetic counselling (brief)
concepts.simple_answer: Couples with family history of genetic disorder may seek counselling to understand risks.
concepts.remember: Science supports medical advice not stigma.

concepts.name: Heredity not determinism
concepts.simple_answer: Genes influence traits but environment, nutrition, and choice also matter especially for complex traits.
concepts.example: Height potential from genes; nutrition affects achieved height.

concepts.name: Class survey activity idea
concepts.simple_answer: Tally inherited traits in class (attached earlobe etc.) — discuss ratios not exact Mendelian in small sample.

concepts.name: Inherited traits summary
concepts.simple_answer: Human traits follow Mendelian principles often simplified; pedigrees, carriers, sex-linked examples extend basics.
concepts.remember: Link to blood groups day before.

concepts.name: Mendel experiment timeline
concepts.simple_answer: P pure lines → F1 cross → F1 self → F2 count — repeat for seven traits and dihybrid.

concepts.name: Seven traits list recall
concepts.simple_answer: Recall pea pairs: stem length, flower colour, pod shape, pod colour, seed shape, seed colour, flower position.
concepts.example: At least four enough for short answers.
concepts.remember: Round/wrinkled and yellow/green seeds common in questions.

concepts.name: Three laws restated
concepts.simple_answer: Dominance; Segregation; Independent Assortment — each with one-sentence meaning and pea evidence.

concepts.name: Why Mendel succeeded — review
concepts.simple_answer: Math, large samples, pure lines, one/two traits isolated, careful record keeping.

concepts.name: Monohybrid ratio recap
concepts.simple_answer: F2 3:1 phenotype; 1:2:1 genotype for single trait heterozygous cross.
concepts.example: Derive from Punnett not rote only.

concepts.name: Dihybrid ratio recap
concepts.simple_answer: F2 9:3:3:1 phenotypes from independently assorting two genes.

concepts.name: Compare monohybrid vs dihybrid
concepts.simple_answer: Monohybrid: one trait, 4 Punnett boxes. Dihybrid: two traits, 16 boxes, independent assortment.
concepts.example: F1 all dominant for both in standard dihybrid start.

concepts.name: NCERT in-text Mendel questions
concepts.simple_answer: Review NCERT questions on Mendel's conclusions and ratio explanations.
concepts.example: Explain why F2 has 3:1 without just stating.

concepts.name: Historical context
concepts.simple_answer: Mendel presented 1865; work ignored then rediscovered — foundation of modern genetics.
concepts.example: Chromosomes and meiosis later explained mechanism.

concepts.name: Mendel review summary
concepts.simple_answer: Pea experiments → three laws → monohybrid 3:1 → dihybrid 9:3:3:1 — full story for board exam.

concepts.name: Activity 8.1 — detailed recap
concepts.simple_answer: Monohybrid simulation with beads/cards: parent alleles in bags, random draw pairs, tally F2 phenotypes over 20+ trials.
concepts.remember: Conclusion: random fusion produces Mendelian ratio approximately.

concepts.name: Activity 8.2 — detailed recap
concepts.simple_answer: Dihybrid simulation: two gene bead sets; combine draws; tally four phenotype classes approaching 9:3:3:1.
concepts.example: More classes than monohybrid — need more trials.

concepts.name: Writing activity conclusions
concepts.simple_answer: Format: Aim, Materials, Procedure, Observation table, Conclusion linking to Mendel laws.
concepts.example: Conclusion must mention ratio and law.
concepts.remember: Observation table with totals and percentages.

concepts.name: Simulation to Punnett link
concepts.simple_answer: Bead draw equals random fertilisation; Punnett square lists all equally likely outcomes theoretically.

concepts.name: Sources of experimental error
concepts.simple_answer: Small trial number deviates from ratio; recording errors; unequal gamete representation if bags wrong.

concepts.name: Class data pooling
concepts.simple_answer: Combine whole class F2 counts — pooled data closer to expected ratio — law of large numbers.
concepts.example: One group's 8:4 may differ; 200 pairs stabilise.

concepts.name: Viva questions for activities
concepts.simple_answer: Prepare: Why 3:1? What is segregation? Why repeat trials? What represents gamete?
concepts.remember: Teacher may ask predict before trial.

concepts.name: Diagram for activity setup
concepts.simple_answer: Sketch bead bags, parent labels Tt, drawing grid for recording offspring genotypes.

concepts.name: Extend activity thinking
concepts.simple_answer: Ask: What if parents TT × tt? Predict F2 if F1 selfed — connect to different starting crosses.
concepts.example: Not all crosses start Tt × Tt.

concepts.name: Activities 8.1–8.2 summary
concepts.simple_answer: Simulations validate Mendel ratios; write full report; link to laws; pool data for accuracy.
concepts.example: Redo simulation at home with coins.

concepts.name: Genotype notation practice
concepts.simple_answer: Write genotypes for homozygous dominant, heterozygous, homozygous recessive using gene symbols T/t, R/r.

concepts.name: Phenotype from genotype rule
concepts.simple_answer: Read phenotype from genotype using dominance rules — TT Tt tall; tt dwarf.
concepts.remember: Write phenotype words not just letters.

concepts.name: Reverse problem — infer genotype
concepts.simple_answer: Given phenotype and parent info infer possible genotypes (carrier detection).
concepts.example: Tall plant could TT or Tt — test cross distinguishes.

concepts.name: Monohybrid mixed problems set
concepts.simple_answer: Solve five crosses: state gametes, Punnett, genotype and phenotype ratios each.

concepts.name: Dihybrid mixed problems set
concepts.simple_answer: Solve two dihybrid crosses fully — 16-box squares.
concepts.remember: Label gametes RY Ry rY ry.

concepts.name: ABO inheritance problem
concepts.simple_answer: Cross type A (Iᴬi) × type B (Iᴮi) — list all child blood groups possible with probabilities.
concepts.example: Four phenotypes possible: A, B, AB, O.

concepts.name: Sex determination problem
concepts.simple_answer: Cross XX × XY — fraction male vs female; explain chromosome contribution.

concepts.name: Word problems
concepts.simple_answer: Parents both heterozygous for unattached earlobe dominant E — fraction homozygous recessive children?

concepts.name: Error checking checklist
concepts.simple_answer: Gametes one allele each; square size correct; ratios count all boxes; phenotype matches dominance.

concepts.name: Genotype/phenotype day summary
concepts.simple_answer: Fluent in Punnett squares mono and dihybrid, ABO, sex crosses — timed practice builds exam speed.

concepts.name: Pea plant trait diagram
concepts.simple_answer: Sketch tall vs dwarf pea, round vs wrinkled seed — label for Mendel experiment context.

concepts.name: Punnett square neat drawing
concepts.simple_answer: Draw 2×2 and 4×4 squares with labelled parent genotypes and gametes on axes.
concepts.remember: Shade or circle genotype classes for counting.

concepts.name: Monohybrid cross figure
concepts.simple_answer: Show P → F1 → F2 generations with genotypes and phenotypes labelled in diagram flow.

concepts.name: Dihybrid cross figure
concepts.simple_answer: Four seed types in F2 grid picture: round-yellow, round-green, wrinkled-yellow, wrinkled-green.

concepts.name: Human sex chromosome diagram
concepts.simple_answer: Draw XX female and XY male karyotype sketch; show egg X and sperm X or Y.

concepts.name: Pedigree chart symbols
concepts.simple_answer: Square male, circle female, filled affected, horizontal mating line, vertical offspring line.

concepts.name: ABO table diagram
concepts.simple_answer: Table: genotype IᴬIᴬ, Iᴬi, etc. mapped to phenotype A, B, AB, O.
concepts.remember: Include in long blood group answer.

concepts.name: Diagram timing practice
concepts.simple_answer: Complete Punnett + sex chromosome + pedigree in 15 minutes total.

concepts.name: Label spelling genetics
concepts.simple_answer: Homozygous, heterozygous, phenotype, genotype, allele, gamete — spell correctly.

concepts.name: Diagram day summary unit 4
concepts.simple_answer: Master Punnett squares, P-F1-F2 flow, sex chromosomes, pedigree — draw without textbook.

concepts.name: 3-mark: Mendel's contribution
concepts.simple_answer: Mendel used pea plants, counted offspring, proposed laws of dominance and segregation explaining F2 3:1 ratio.

concepts.name: 3-mark: Dominant vs recessive
concepts.simple_answer: Define with example; dominant expresses in heterozygote; recessive needs homozygous; pea tall/dwarf.

concepts.name: 5-mark: Monohybrid cross explanation
concepts.simple_answer: Describe Mendel monohybrid experiment P F1 F2 with diagram Punnett and 3:1 ratio explanation via segregation.

concepts.name: 5-mark: Dihybrid and independent assortment
concepts.simple_answer: Explain dihybrid cross, F2 9:3:3:1, state law of independent assortment with gamete types.

concepts.name: 5-mark: Sex determination humans
concepts.simple_answer: Explain XX XY system, role of father sperm, Punnett square, dispel myths.

concepts.name: 5-mark: Blood group inheritance
concepts.simple_answer: Explain multiple alleles, codominance AB, sample cross predicting offspring groups.

concepts.name: NCERT exercise long questions
concepts.simple_answer: Practice textbook end questions on Mendel laws, variation accumulation, and sex determination.

concepts.name: Assertion-reason heredity
concepts.simple_answer: Practice AR: e.g. assertion F1 all dominant phenotype — reason segregation of alleles in gametes.
concepts.example: Both statements may be true independently.

concepts.name: Previous year themes Ch 8
concepts.simple_answer: Recurring: 3:1 and 9:3:3:1 ratios, sex determination, ABO cross, Mendel's laws list.

concepts.name: Written prep summary unit 4
concepts.simple_answer: Prepare 3 short + 4 long templates covering Mendel, crosses, sex, blood groups.

concepts.name: Ch 8 key terms set 1
concepts.simple_answer: Heredity, variation, gene, allele, dominant, recessive, genotype, phenotype, homozygous, heterozygous.

concepts.name: Ch 8 key terms set 2
